headline: IBM researchers used teams of AI agents running on open models to design a chip for decoding quantum errors, at a fraction of the usual AI cost.
score_reason: Research preprint of interest to quantum and AI engineers; savings are the authors own figures.
importance_line: It suggests AI agents could help design the specialised classical chips that error-corrected quantum computers need, which matters to quantum and chip engineers, but the figures are the authors' own and apply to one decoder design.
summary: Quantum Computing Report reports that IBM Research used an "agent factory" of cooperating AI agents on open-weight models to design hardware for a quantum error-correction decoder, cutting AI inference costs by 11.5 times and reaching up to a 204 times hardware speedup. In the all-open setup, a 52 times speedup cost $26 in inference, according to the authors' paper.
notes: Read Quantum Computing Report article via curl (fulltext file was empty). Paper not read directly. Authors named in the article include Abhishek Bhandwaldar, Mihir Choudhury and Ruchir Puri; roles not stated, so not named in the entry.
